title: Reproduce user-visible data bugs before asking the user to re-verify
summary: When a user reports that a data-backed UI still shows the wrong count, stale placement, or unchanged result after a fix, an agent may keep asking the user to click again instead of reproducing the exact data path. The safer pattern is to run the same read/query/apply/readback loop against representative data, then ask the user only for information the agent cannot observe.
ai_value: Reduces user frustration and catches mismatches between the intended model, the query predicate, and the rendered state. It also prevents agents from mistaking a successful unit test or code review for evidence that the operator-visible data path is fixed.

contexts: Rule engines, filters, labels, folders, queues, dashboards, and bulk actions
Bugs where the user's observable count, row placement, or detail view disagrees with the agent's expected state

trigger_signals.description: The user says a fixed rule still matches zero rows, the row remains in the old place, or the UI still shows stale labels/counts after applying the change.
trigger_signals.agent_interpretation: Stop relying on the previous code-level check. Reproduce the exact user-visible data path and collect readback evidence.

trigger_signals.description: The implementation has separate preview, apply, receive-time, and detail/list queries that are supposed to share semantics.
trigger_signals.agent_interpretation: Verify semantic parity across the paths rather than testing only one helper or endpoint.

negative_signals.description: The user-visible issue depends on credentials, live data, or privacy-sensitive facts the agent is not authorized to access.
negative_signals.why_it_matters: Do not bypass access boundaries. Ask for the minimal missing observation or route through an approved debug path instead.

negative_signals.description: A deterministic local fixture reproduces the exact query/apply/render path and has already been run after the disputed fix.
negative_signals.why_it_matters: A fixture can replace live-data readback when it covers the same predicates and state transitions.

common_wrong_assumptions: A passing unit test proves the operator-visible list is fixed.
If the helper function was corrected, preview, apply, receive-time, and detail views must all agree.
The user can cheaply verify one more time, so asking again is acceptable.
A zero-match result means there is no matching data, not that the query normalized the scope incorrectly.
A secondary label or stale relationship means the primary visible location is already correct.

first_checks.check: Identify the exact state the user expected to change: source predicate, destination/visible location, count, and the page or endpoint that displays it.
first_checks.why: Without the observable success state, the agent may verify a different path than the one the user is judging.

first_checks.check: Run a read-only count/readback query before mutation or against a fixture: source candidates, already-applied exclusions, and destination inventory.
first_checks.why: This separates no data, wrong scope normalization, and wrong already-applied predicates.

first_checks.check: After apply, re-read through the same data path the UI uses, not only through the helper that performed the write.
first_checks.why: Many bugs live in list/detail/read models rather than the write function.

first_checks.check: If asking the user again is unavoidable, include what the agent already verified and the one observation that remains inaccessible.
first_checks.why: This keeps the user from becoming the default test harness and makes the remaining gap explicit.

decision_rules.condition: The agent can access representative data or a faithful fixture safely.
decision_rules.then: Reproduce the failure with count/readback evidence, fix the predicate or state transition, and verify the same path after the change before asking for user confirmation.

decision_rules.condition: The path touches private live data or credentials outside the agent's grant.
decision_rules.then: Do not broaden access. Ask only for the smallest screenshot/count/log needed, or route through an authorized readback/debug workflow.

do_not: Do not ask the user to repeatedly test the same path while the agent has safe access to reproduce it.
Do not treat a helper-level unit test as proof that the rendered list, detail page, and counts agree.
Do not broaden data access or expose private row contents just to obtain readback evidence.
Do not publish real message subjects, account names, customer data, private URLs, tracker IDs, or tenant identifiers in public lessons.

agent_directives.preferred_next_step: For user-visible data bugs, write down the observable success state, then run a safe count/apply/readback loop against representative data before returning to the user.

risk.notes: The diagnostic pattern is safe when it stays read-only or uses authorized reversible test data. Live mutations, private data access, credentials, or irreversible actions still require the normal gate for that system.

sources.supports: A private agent session initially relied on code-level fixes and user retesting for a rule/list mismatch. The issue was resolved only after running representative apply/readback checks that exposed scope normalization and already-applied predicate bugs.
